name: Jones's Grocery and Provision Store
aka: H. Jones's grocery and provision store

documented_range.note: THE START IS THE FIRST DATE A CONTEMPORARY DOCUMENT PUTS THE BUSINESS IN CHICAGO. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 carries a display advertisement headed 'Grocery & Provision Store. B. JONES. CHICAGO-ILLINOIS.' — which is primary evidence that a Jones grocery was trading in the town on that day. Andreas independently records 'grocery and provision store and forwarding and commission store by H. Jones' among the 1834 advertisers. THAT IS EVIDENCE ABOUT A BUSINESS AND NOT ABOUT A BUILDING; nothing reached dates the premises at either end, and the range closes at the end of the scene year on the ordinary continuity cut.

position.symbolic_location: South side of South Water Street just east of Wells Street (today the south side of West Wacker Drive) — the street is attested, the block is not.
position.note: CONJECTURAL, AND ONLY THE STREET IS EVIDENCE. Andreas places Jones among the South Water Street district advertisers and this project's dossier records the block as unattested; the contemporary advertisement of 26 November 1833 gives no address at all beyond 'Chicago-Illinois'. The point recorded here is at the west end of the Wells-to-LaSalle block, on the south side, and NOTHING SUPPORTS THAT CHOICE OF BLOCK — it is a lot on the right street with room on it, which is a rendering decision and not a finding. THE ALONG-STREET UNCERTAINTY IS THE WHOLE STREET, about 630 m from Market to State. THE SIDE OF THE STREET IS REASONED: the north side of South Water was the river bank, wharves and landings (docs/research/04-structures-south.md § 12), so a store is on the south side. METHOD, for the cross-street position only: the modern West Upper Wacker Drive centreline was interpolated between the intersection centres at North Wells (EPSG:26916 E 447402.5, N 4637411.6) and North LaSalle (E 447525.2, N 4637408.1), read from OpenStreetMap 2026-08-11, and the south kerb taken 12.2 m south of it as half an 80 ft platted street. Working uncertainty about 20 m across the street from the georeference (data/datum.json, 17.5 m RMS) and the length of the street along it. Facade bearing 0, north onto South Water, inferred from the street rather than from any statement. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-27 (T-0199), AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE — ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above set this footprint's north face on the South Water frontage, and it found that frontage by taking the MODERN West Wacker Drive centreline out of OpenStreetMap and stepping 12.2 m south of it. That is not this project's own South Water Street: the committed centreline in data/streets/1835.json, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what tools/generate_plat_lots.py builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it, this record's north wall stood 8.17 m OUT PAST the blk_south_water_wells frontage line, in the platted roadway — far enough into it that tools/generate_frontage_works.py refused the plank sidewalk along this stretch of South Water in writing and named this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 9.67 m along the face's inward normal — dE +0.079 m, dN -9.671 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447420.0 N 4637391.3 becomes E 447420.079 N 4637381.629 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin tools/generate_block_infill.py gives every reconstructed unit standing on this face, and the same repair the six reconciled under T-0198 carry. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence. WHY IT TOOK A SECOND RUN, AND WHOSE DECISION IT WAS. T-0198 measured this exact translation and REFUSED to apply it, for a reason that was real: reconciled onto the plat this building SEATS on lot 0 of blk_south_water_wells, and that lot is one the 665-roof schedule had already dealt to the anonymous South Water frontage run, which tools/generate_block_infill.py refused — one principal roof to a lot. Nothing overlapped; the worst overlap between any of the eleven South Water placements and any committed footprint in the town is zero. What refused this repair was a RULE about entitlement, not the ground. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-08-27 that a platted business-front lot may carry a documented store at the street AND an anonymous dwelling behind it, on the reasoning that the geometry already permits it and the alternative pays eight roofs and two households for a rule the corrected data had itself called into question. The clause and its three tests are written into tools/plat_occupancy.py; no roof left the town and no household moved. WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 359.53 (i.e. -0.47), so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.60 m at the other. That skew is smaller than the walk's own daylight and it is not corrected here, because rotating a documented record is a second claim and this one is a repair.

derivation.reason: This placement predates the derivation module. Its provenance and reasoning are recorded in position.note, but no machine-checkable derivation block has been authored for it yet.

footprint.note: INVENTED — the parcel's borrowed rectangle, 12.192 x 7.62 m = 40 x 25 ft, from the Green Tree Tavern's attested frontage and room module. Nothing is attested about this building. The larger rather than the smaller rectangle is used because Andreas describes the business as a grocery and provision store AND a forwarding and commission store, which is two trades under one roof and wants floor for barrels — an argument about the trade, not about the building. The documented South Water lot width of 55 ft is a cap and 40 ft sits inside it.

stories.note: Nothing is attested. One is recorded because it is the smaller claim. Invention, tagged as such.

construction.note: Not stated. Frame rather than log because this project's dossier records the mid-1830s South Water commercial stock as frame and because a provision store wants clear floor and a wide door. Braced rather than balloon frame follows the Sauganash record's argument; nothing decides between them.

wall_height_m.note: No figure is attested. 3.6 m is about 12 ft, one storey built taller than a dwelling's for stacked goods and a cart door. It inherits the storey count's uncertainty, which is conjectural.

roof_type.note: Not attested. Gable is the near-universal roof form for frame buildings of this type, period and region.

roof_pitch_deg.note: No pitch is attested for this building. 33 degrees is the frame_storefront archetype's own figure for a store, and it is adopted here rather than the 38 this project uses for taverns because the archetype argues the case from the dataset's one attested store footprint: a store's frontage is long and its plan shallow, so a tavern's pitch puts more roof above the eave than there is wall below it and the building stops reading as a shop. Inferred from construction practice and from the type, not measured.

chimneys.note: Not attested. One is the minimum for a store kept through Chicago winters. The COUNT is the inference; the stack's position, size and material are the archetype's, per docs/LIBERTIES.md L26.

dock.note: RECONSTRUCTED, UNDER THE OWNER'S RULING OF 2026-08-18 — 'you can add more docks!', given with the general instruction to be liberal with reconstructed items and label them as such (T-0062; data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md). NO SOURCE STATES A DOCK, WHARF OR LANDING AT THIS FRONTAGE — that absence is exactly why this value is reconstructed and not inferred, one tier below the two river warehouses whose dock is stated in the dossier. What bounds the invention: (1) THE TRADE — a grocery and provision store advertising from the Chicago Democrat's first number in November 1833, and by 1834 doing forwarding and commission work as well (Andreas) — the second half of that trade is the same argument as J. H. Kinzie's. (2) THE REACH — this building stands on the South Water river frontage between the forks and the Dearborn drawbridge, the working bank the 2026-08-18 brief shows crowded with masts (image 3) and the reach every schooner cargo landed on; a street of merchants whose whole stock came in by water did not work it over two landings. (3) THE PRACTICE — wharfing-out along the south bank is the practice T-0041's research note records as the thing that would move this layer off reconstruction, and the docks it drew are this landing's pattern. The landing itself is the wharf layer's standard form (data/wharves/river_landings.json, tools/generate_river_wharves.py), every dimension invented within the bounds L132 states; geometry 'simplified' is the exact claim — a standard-form landing stands for a statement this record cannot make from evidence. Claimed at docs/LIBERTIES.md L145. The Temple Building on the same frontage gets NO landing from the same rule: worship and a school take nothing off a schooner.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this record wears 4.5 in — dealt by tools/deal_siding_stock.py: keyed to the phase's construction season, because buildings sided from the same season's shipments of St Joseph sawn lumber tend toward one stock, then advanced so no frame building within 60 m shares this one's. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention.

phases.change_note: A grocery and provision store kept by Jones on South Water Street — one of the businesses advertising in the first number of the Chicago Democrat in November 1833 and still among the town's advertisers in 1834, by which time Andreas has it doing forwarding and commission work as well.

function.note: Documented twice and once contemporaneously: the advertisement in the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is headed 'Grocery & Provision Store', and Andreas records the same trade with forwarding and commission added by 1834. The trade is the best-evidenced thing about this record.

occupants.note: THE INITIAL DISAGREES BETWEEN THE TWO SOURCES AND THE RECORD DOES NOT PICK ONE. Andreas writes 'H. Jones'. The advertisement in the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 reads 'B. JONES'. A contemporary advertisement is the man's own word about his own name and would normally win outright, but the reading comes off a scan of a damaged sheet, the letters B and H are among the easiest to confuse in a display face of this period, and this project has been warned that the transcription accompanying the scan is imperfect elsewhere in the same issue. So the surname is carried, the initial is not, and the record id keeps the H that this project's dossier assigned it because renaming a record is worse than annotating one. Both readings are recorded in aka.

research_note: A CONTEMPORARY ADVERTISEMENT AND NO ADDRESS, which is the shape of most of the weak tier of this street. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 proves a Jones grocery and provision store was trading at Chicago on that day; Andreas puts the same trade among the 1834 South Water advertisers and adds forwarding and commission. Neither says where. Position and footprint are conjectural, storeys with them, and the record is a business placed on the right street. THE INITIAL IS AN OPEN QUESTION, recorded on occupants: Andreas says H. Jones, the scan says B. JONES, and this record carries both rather than choosing. That is the kind of disagreement the project's honesty rules exist for — a single letter, on a damaged sheet, between a contemporary document and a compilation fifty years later. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE THIS RECORD: any 1834-35 advertisement carrying Jones's address, which Andreas's own 1834 summary implies exists in the Democrat's files; or a clean reading of the 26 November 1833 sheet's advertisement block, which would at least settle the initial. See docs/RESEARCH/h_jones_store.md.
